final_answer: A hash table handles collisions by using methods like chaining or open addressing to resolve conflicts when two keys hash to the same index in the array. Chaining involves storing multiple elements in the same index using a linked list or other data structure, which can lead to higher memory usage but simpler implementation. Open addressing, on the other hand, uses probing techniques like linear probing or quadratic probing to find the next available slot, which can lead to better cache performance but more complex code. Chaining is generally easier to implement and can handle more elements without significant performance degradation, whereas open addressing may suffer from clustering and requires careful tuning of probe sequences to maintain efficiency.
